chapter: Gambling, Cab's small groups and Havana
title: Cab's seven-piece band, the Palomar Club in Vancouver and a salmon fish fry
summary: After Cab cut down to seven pieces they played Vancouver, where Francis caught salmon, and later went down to four.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: And then Cab broke up the big band and went down to 7 pieces, didn't he?
Yeah, 7 pieces.
Yeah.
That was when we played up in Canada, and I went fishing and caught those salmon that came back and ...
What was the name of that club there?
The Palimar.
The Palimar Club in Vancouver, right?
(Willie Smith)
Vancouver, right. It was owned by this guy named Sandy Desantis. And Sammy Davis and his father and uncle were playing at the Cave at the same time we were there.
At the Cave, that's right.
And that night after work, we had a big fish fry, everybody was there.
Yeah, you had caught that salmon.
Yeah, I caught some salmon when I went fishing.
Yeah. Now that 7 piece band was composed of Sam Taylor, Keg Ray Johnson and Jonah Jones. And you David and Francis on drums, and Dave Rivera on piano.
Yeah, and Milt Hinton on bass and Cab Calloway. Yeah.
We played all out in the west, too.
That's right.
Yeah, San Francisco ...
All out in California, right. Yeah.
And we kept that band -- oh, I don't remember how long that band stayed together, but we stayed together a couple of years or so.
Yeah, I think it was a couple of years, and then he cut down to four.
Down to four pieces.
